prompt: Design the cryptography for a versioned encrypted document format. Each document belongs to a tenant and has document ID, format version, content type, and creation sequence. A random data-encryption key is supplied by the key-management layer; the application must choose the AEAD envelope, nonce strategy safe across process restart, concurrent writers, VM snapshot/clone, and key rotation, associated data, serialized fields, key/algorithm identifiers, tamper behavior, and migration from version 1 to future algorithms. Use standard library constructions, never process unauthenticated plaintext as valid content, and define negative cases for nonce reuse, ciphertext/tag tamper, metadata substitution between tenant/document IDs, truncation, wrong key/version, and downgrade. KMS generation/wrapping/rotation is out of scope.

requirements: document envelope fixture with tenant/document/version metadata

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The format uses a standard AEAD construction with explicit algorithm/key identifiers and rejects authentication failure before treating decrypted bytes as trusted content.

Nonce generation/allocation has an explicit uniqueness argument under each key that covers concurrent writers, restart, cloned/snapshotted state, and key rotation rather than relying on an unqualified random-nonce assumption.

Tenant/document identity, format/version, and other immutable meaning-changing metadata are cryptographically bound through associated data or the authenticated envelope so ciphertext cannot be transplanted between domains.
The serialized envelope has an unambiguous canonical/versioned field representation and validates lengths/algorithm IDs before cryptographic processing without permitting attacker-selected downgrade.
The design explains how old records are recognized, decrypted, and migrated/re-encrypted under later algorithms/keys while preserving authenticated version semantics.
